findings.summary: Monotonic guard mixes two different clocks (Yorkie `issuedAt` vs. backend `now()`), so a backend-side bump can permanently block later webhook bumps under clock skew
findings.evidence: `touchUpdatedAt` only advances when `updatedAt < at` (document.service.ts:121), but `at` comes from Yorkie's clock (`Date.parse(issuedAt)`), while `DocumentService.updateDocument` (document.service.ts:100) and the NaN/clamp fallback here write the *backend's* `new Date()`. If the Yorkie server clock lags the backend's by N (or a rename happens at backend-now while Yorkie is behind), every subsequent `DocumentRootChanged` carries an `issuedAt` less than the stored value and is silently dropped — the doc stops floating on edits for the whole skew window, with no log and a 200 response. The design doc only reasons about *future* skew; the symmetric past-skew case is unhandled. A safer form is `at = max(issuedAt-clamped, ...)` or simply always writing backend `now()` for received events.

findings.summary: Only `NaN` is treated as a missing `issuedAt`; a zero/epoch or absurdly-old timestamp is accepted and silently produces a no-op update
findings.evidence: `const issuedMs = Date.parse(body.attributes?.issuedAt ?? '')` then `Number.isNaN(issuedMs) ? now : Math.min(issuedMs, now)`. Yorkie's Go zero time serializes as `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`, which `Date.parse` returns a large *negative* number for — not NaN. That value passes the clamp, and `touchUpdatedAt`'s `updatedAt: { lt: at }` predicate then matches nothing, so the edit is swallowed with a 200 and `updatedAt` never advances. The repo's own sibling parser explicitly guards this case (`yorkie-admin.service.ts:274`: `if (Number.isNaN(ms) || ms <= 0) return undefined`); this new parser does not. Same class of silent drop for any implausibly old timestamp.

findings.summary: Raw-body capture keys off an exact `req.url` string match while Express routes the same endpoint far more leniently — any trailing slash, case difference, duplicated slash or path prefix makes every webhook 401 and silently disables the feature
findings.evidence: `if (req.url?.split('?', 1)[0] === YORKIE_WEBHOOK_PATH) req.rawBody = buf;` compares byte-for-byte against '/internal/yorkie/events'. Express's default routing is case-insensitive and non-strict about trailing slashes, so `POST /internal/yorkie/events/` or `/Internal/Yorkie/Events` reaches `YorkieEventController.handleEvent` but arrives with `rawBody === undefined`; `yorkie-signature.guard.ts:49` then throws UnauthorizedException for every delivery. The failure mode is invisible (guard logs nothing for the missing-rawBody branch, and `updatedAt` simply never advances). The registered URL is an ops-supplied string (docs/design/documents-last-modified.md:69), and nothing verifies the coupling: the e2e harness never applies this middleware — `test/helpers/integration-helpers.ts:75 applyGlobalBootstrap` installs only the ValidationPipe — so no test exercises rawBody capture end to end. Prefer a case-insensitive/normalized prefix match (or capture on the route via middleware bound to the controller path).

findings.summary: A database failure in `touchUpdatedAt` escapes as a 500, contradicting the controller's stated "always 200 so Yorkie won't retry" contract
findings.evidence: `await this.documentService.touchUpdatedAt(parsed.id, at)` is unguarded, while the class doc (lines 9-12) says "we would rather swallow-and-200 anything we don't recognize than trigger a retry storm" and the spec asserts 'always answers ok so Yorkie does not retry'. A transient Prisma/Postgres error therefore returns 500 and triggers Yorkie's retry-with-backoff for every in-flight edit event — precisely the retry storm the comment claims to avoid — with no local log of the failure. Either catch+log and return `{ ok: true }`, or drop the claim from the docs/tests.

findings.summary: `updateDocument`'s new "bump only when data is non-empty" heuristic counts keys, not defined values, so an all-`undefined` update body still bumps `updatedAt`
findings.evidence: `document.service.ts:100` decides via `Object.keys(data).length > 0`. The api/v1 PATCH passes the request body straight through (`data: body`), and that route has no DTO class, so a body such as `{"title": null}` / `{"title": undefined}`-shaped payloads yield `Object.keys(...).length === 1` and re-sort the document to the top of the list even though nothing changed — the exact scenario the new empty-data guard and its unit test claim to prevent. Filtering on defined values (or bumping only in the controllers that know a real field changed) would be consistent.

findings.summary: List ordering has no final unique tiebreak, so documents sharing an identical `updatedAt`/`createdAt` (e.g. all rows right after the backfill migration) come back in an unspecified, potentially varying Postgres order
findings.evidence: `orderBy: [{ updatedAt: 'desc' }, { createdAt: 'desc' }]` — after `migration.sql` sets `updatedAt = createdAt` for every existing row, both keys tie for any rows created in the same millisecond, and Postgres may return ties in different orders across plans/polls. This is the same visible symptom (list reshuffling between polls) that the change set out to fix. Adding `{ id: 'desc' }` as the last key makes the order total.

findings.summary: The PR's headline behavior — list `updatedAt`/ordering now sourced from Postgres, editors from the best-effort Yorkie call — has no test at all
findings.evidence: `attachMeta` was rewritten (updatedAt from `d.updatedAt.toISOString()`, editors from `yorkieAdminService.getEditors`) and both list endpoints changed to `orderBy: [{updatedAt:'desc'},{createdAt:'desc'}]`. The only controller spec, packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.spec.ts, covers solely `createDocument` fileId gating and still constructs the controller with a `{ getSummaries: jest.fn() }` stub (line 13) — it never calls attachMeta/listDocuments. Nothing asserts that a Yorkie failure/timeout leaves order intact (the stated motivation), that editors are attached from the new map shape, or that the orderBy array is passed to the service. I grepped packages/backend for `attachMeta`/`orderBy`/`getEditors` and read the controller spec and all packages/backend/test e2e specs (authenticated-http, api-key-http, document-file-serving) — no coverage.

findings.summary: `touchUpdatedAt`'s monotonic/idempotent guard (`updatedAt: { lt: at }`) is untested
findings.evidence: The new `touchUpdatedAt` uses `updateMany({ where: { id, updatedAt: { lt: at } } })` and returns the row count — the doc comment claims idempotence, monotonicity and silent no-op for a missing document, which is the whole safety story for at-least-once/out-of-order webhook delivery. The new packages/backend/src/document/document.service.spec.ts only mocks `{ document: { update } }` and tests `updateDocument`; it never mocks `updateMany` or calls `touchUpdatedAt`. The webhook spec mocks `touchUpdatedAt` away entirely, so no test would fail if the `lt` predicate were dropped or inverted (i.e. if a stale duplicate delivery could move updatedAt backwards). Searched packages/backend for `touchUpdatedAt` — only the service, the webhook controller, and the webhook spec's mock.

findings.summary: Raw-body capture wiring (path-scoped `verify` hook) is never exercised; the guard spec injects `rawBody` by hand, so a wrong path constant would ship green
findings.evidence: The HMAC check depends entirely on `req.rawBody` being populated only for `/internal/yorkie/events` by the bodyParser `verify` hook in main.ts. yorkie-signature.guard.spec.ts fabricates the request (`contextFor(rawBody, signature)`, lines 22-33), so it proves nothing about the wiring: if YORKIE_WEBHOOK_PATH did not match the controller route (`internal/yorkie` + `events`, possibly plus a global prefix), or if the mount order left rawBody unset, every real webhook would 401 and all tests would still pass. No e2e/integration spec hits `/internal/yorkie/events` — grepped packages for `internal/yorkie` and `rawBody`; matches only in main.ts, the controller, the guard and the guard spec.

findings.summary: Test titled 'always answers ok so Yorkie does not retry' only covers the early-return path; the interesting failure path (touchUpdatedAt rejecting) is untested and would in fact 500
findings.evidence: The test calls `handleEvent({ type: 'DocumentRootChanged' })` with no `attributes`, which returns early before touching the service — so it asserts the trivial branch while claiming the general 'never retry' guarantee. `handleEvent` has no try/catch around `await this.documentService.touchUpdatedAt(...)`, and no test makes the mock reject, so the assertion cannot support its stated intent.

findings.summary: Test claims 'missing or unparseable' issuedAt but only exercises the missing case
findings.evidence: The it() title is 'falls back to now() when issuedAt is missing or unparseable', yet the body only sends `{ key: 'sheet-xyz' }` with no issuedAt. No case passes a garbage string (e.g. 'not-a-date'), so the `Number.isNaN(Date.parse(...))` branch on a present-but-invalid value is only covered incidentally via the same code path.

findings.summary: `getEditors` (the new projection the controller now depends on) has no unit test
findings.evidence: yorkie-admin.service.spec.ts tests only `projectSummary` and `parseTimestamp` (grep of describe/it in that file). `getEditors` filters out documents with zero editors and returns an empty map when getSummaries fails/has no secret — behavior the controller relies on for `item.editors` — with no test. (This function is in the working tree but not shown in the diff, so it may be pre-existing; flagging in case it arrived with this branch.)

findings.summary: Migration backfill (`UPDATE Document SET updatedAt = createdAt`) has no coverage in the Postgres integration lane
findings.evidence: No test asserts that pre-existing rows come back ordered by their creation time after migration; searched packages/backend/test for `updatedAt` (matches only in unrelated e2e specs) and found no migration-level assertion. Hard to unit test, hence nit.

findings.summary: Data-model + API change not folded into the canonical backend design doc; a new parallel top-level doc was created instead
findings.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md:55-59 requires architecture/data-model changes to live in the design docs and to "Update the existing doc when evolving an area instead of creating parallel files." `docs/design/backend.md` is the canonical doc for "NestJS modules, API reference, auth system, database schema" (README.md:109), yet its Database Schema ER block (backend.md:315-319) still lists Document with `createdAt` only, its module table (backend.md:70) still says DocumentModule = "Document REST endpoints" with no YorkieEventController, and its API reference has no `POST /internal/yorkie/events` entry. The change instead adds a wholly new top-level `docs/design/documents-last-modified.md` covering the same subsystem.

findings.summary: Dead second source of truth for last-modified left behind (getSummaries/DocumentSummary.updatedAt) with now-stale doc comments
findings.evidence: After this change no production code reads a Yorkie last-modified time: `document.controller.ts` and `api/v1/documents.controller.ts` both call `getEditors`, which discards `summary.updatedAt` (yorkie-admin.service.ts:108-116). `getSummaries`' doc comment still advertises "last-modified time … letting callers fall back to Postgres data" (lines 74-77) and `projectSummary` still parses `updatedAt` (line 262). Frontend `document-list-utils.ts:41` likewise still documents the value as "Yorkie's `updatedAt`". Two last-modified pipelines now coexist, only one live.

findings.summary: Yorkie webhook controller + signature guard placed in DocumentModule rather than the existing yorkie module
findings.evidence: All other Yorkie integration code lives in `packages/backend/src/yorkie/` (`yorkie-admin.service.ts`, `yorkie-doc-key.ts`). The new `internal/yorkie` controller and `YorkieSignatureGuard` are added under `src/document/` and registered in `document.module.ts`, splitting the Yorkie boundary across two modules; the guard also reads `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY`, the yorkie module's config.

findings.summary: `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY` env documentation not updated for its new, harder requirement
findings.evidence: README.md:38-41 still describes the key as "Optional … enables 'currently editing' presence … Omit and the list still works without avatars." With this change an unset key makes `POST /internal/yorkie/events` return 503 (yorkie-signature.guard.ts:33-41), so last-modified ordering silently never advances. The env doc (and the design doc's ops section) do not record this new consequence.

findings.summary: Public REST API v1 document list neither orders by nor documents the new `updatedAt` field
findings.evidence: `ApiV1DocumentsController.list` returns raw Prisma rows, so the new `Document.updatedAt` column now appears in the v1 response as an undocumented additive field while the list keeps its unspecified default ordering — inconsistent with the app list's new `[{updatedAt: desc}, {createdAt: desc}]`. `docs/design/rest-api.md` is not updated (its only `createdAt` mention is the ApiKey model, line 61).

findings.summary: New design doc deviates from docs/design/template.md heading structure
findings.evidence: template.md prescribes `## Summary`, `### Goals`, `### Non-Goals`, `## Proposal Details`, `### Risks and Mitigation`. The new doc merges goals into one `## Goals / Non-Goals` heading and promotes `## Risks and Mitigation` to a top-level section, plus adds unspecified `### Ops` / `### Clock skew` subsections.

findings.summary: Issue outcome only half-delivered in-repo: the webhook is never registered by anything in the change
findings.evidence: The todo's own unchecked task (line 50-52) and the design doc's Ops section admit that until a manual `yorkie project update --event-webhook-url …` runs, `updatedAt` never advances — i.e. the shipped code delivers stability but not the "still reflects real edit recency" goal (documents-last-modified.md:29). Nothing in the repo (helm chart, compose, migration, bootstrap script) registers the webhook, so no reviewable artifact backs the ops step.

findings.summary: New unauthenticated webhook endpoint is exempted from rate limiting (`@SkipThrottle`) while the body is fully parsed (up to 25MB) and the raw bytes retained *before* the HMAC guard runs — unauthenticated DoS amplification
findings.evidence: `@SkipThrottle()` (yorkie-event.controller.ts:32) removes the only global rate limit (`APP_GUARD: ThrottlerGuard`, app.module.ts:113, 120 req/min) from `POST /internal/yorkie/events`. That route has no JWT guard; the only auth is `YorkieSignatureGuard`, and Nest guards run *after* Express middleware. So the ordering for an anonymous attacker is: body-parser buffers and JSON-parses up to `JSON_BODY_LIMIT` = 25MB (main.ts:20,49), the `verify` hook additionally retains the full raw Buffer for exactly this path (main.ts:51-52), and only then does the guard reject with 401. An attacker with no credentials can therefore pin CPU (25MB JSON.parse) and hold 2x25MB per concurrent request, unbounded in rate, against a route that is on the same public listener as the rest of the API (no `setGlobalPrefix`, no ingress/NetworkPolicy in the repo restricts `/internal/*` — the design doc's "internal cluster URL, no public exposure" is an ops assumption, not enforced in code). Suggested hardening: a dedicated small body limit for this path and a throttle bucket instead of a blanket `@SkipThrottle`.

findings.summary: Mass assignment into the `DocumentService.updateDocument` sink touched by this diff: the v1 API PATCH forwards the raw request body as the Prisma update payload, allowing arbitrary scalar columns (`workspaceId`, `authorID`, `fileId`) to be set
findings.evidence: `ApiV1DocumentsController.update` types the body as an inline object literal (`@Body() body: { title?: string }`, line 71) — a non-class metatype, so the global `ValidationPipe({whitelist, forbidNonWhitelisted})` in main.ts:60 does not strip anything — and passes it straight through as `data: body` (line 79) into `DocumentService.updateDocument`, which this diff rewrote (document.service.ts:88-102) and which spreads it into `prisma.document.update({data: {...data, updatedAt}})`. Prisma validates `update.data` at runtime against the checked *or* unchecked input shape, so an attacker holding an API key / membership for workspace A can send `{"workspaceId":"<workspace they control>"}` to move a document out of A into their own workspace, `{"authorID":n}` to reassign ownership, or `{"fileId":"<victim's blob id>"}` — and then read the other tenant's PDF bytes through `GET documents/:id/file`, which only checks membership of the *document's* workspace before streaming `doc.fileId` (document-file.controller.ts:48-53). Pre-existing code, not introduced here, but it is the unguarded call site of the update path this change modified; the fix is a validated DTO or an explicit field allow-list as `DocumentController.updateDocument` (document.controller.ts:183-191) already does.

findings.summary: Webhook signature covers only the body — no timestamp/nonce replay window, so a captured signed request can be replayed indefinitely
findings.evidence: `YorkieSignatureGuard.canActivate` computes `HMAC-SHA256(rawBody)` and compares (lines 53-61) with no freshness check; the controller reads `issuedAt` from the body but only uses it as the value to store (yorkie-event.controller.ts:56-58), never to reject stale deliveries. Anyone who observes one signed request (internal network capture, proxy/CDN log, mirrored traffic) can replay it forever. Blast radius is small because `touchUpdatedAt` is monotonic (`updatedAt: { lt: at }`, document.service.ts:121) so a replay is a no-op after the first apply, but there is also nothing bounding replay volume since the route is `@SkipThrottle`. Rejecting `issuedAt` older than a few minutes would close it.

findings.summary: Webhook body fields are typed but never validated at runtime; a non-string `attributes.key` throws an unhandled TypeError inside `parseYorkieDocKey`, producing a 500 on a route deliberately designed to always return 200
findings.evidence: `YorkieEventBody` is an interface (yorkie-event.controller.ts:14-17), so the global `ValidationPipe` has no metatype to validate and the body is accepted verbatim. Line 45 does `key ? parseYorkieDocKey(key) : null`; for `{"attributes":{"key":{}}}` or `{"key":123}` the truthiness check passes and `key.startsWith(prefix)` (yorkie-doc-key.ts:50) throws `TypeError` → 500, defeating the controller's stated "200-swallow so Yorkie won't retry" contract and turning a malformed delivery into a retry storm. Requires a valid HMAC signature to reach, so it is post-auth (hence minor), but `typeof key !== 'string'` is a one-line guard.

findings.summary: Raw-body capture keys off an exact, case-sensitive `req.url` string comparison that does not match Express's own (case-insensitive, trailing-slash-tolerant) routing, so several request forms reach the guard with no `rawBody`
findings.evidence: main.ts:51 captures `rawBody` only when `req.url.split('?',1)[0] === '/internal/yorkie/events'`. Express routing by default is case-insensitive and non-strict, so `/Internal/Yorkie/Events` and `/internal/yorkie/events/` route to the same handler but skip the capture; the guard then throws `UnauthorizedException('Missing webhook signature')` (yorkie-signature.guard.ts:49-50). This is fail-closed, so it is not a bypass — the risk is the inverse: the coupling is invisible and silently breaks (every webhook 401s) if a `setGlobalPrefix`, proxy path rewrite, or controller path change is ever introduced, and the mismatch is only detectable in production. Matching on the parsed/normalized path, or scoping the parser with `app.use(PATH, bodyParser.json({verify}))`, removes the footgun.

findings.summary: Guard distinguishes "secret not configured" (503) from "bad signature" (401) to unauthenticated callers, leaking backend configuration state
findings.evidence: `canActivate` throws `ServiceUnavailableException('Webhook verification unavailable')` when `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY` is unset (lines 34-41) and `UnauthorizedException` otherwise, on a route with no other authentication. Since `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY` is documented as optional (packages/backend/README.md:38), an anonymous probe of `/internal/yorkie/events` reliably reveals whether the deployment has a Yorkie project secret provisioned. Returning 401 in both cases (and logging the config error server-side, which it already does) avoids the oracle.

findings.summary: Nothing in the repo registers the Yorkie project event webhook, so every environment that isn't manually reconfigured silently loses "Last modified"
findings.evidence: The list's `updatedAt` now comes only from `Document.updatedAt`, which is advanced solely by `POST /internal/yorkie/events` (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-event.controller.ts:38). The only Yorkie deployment artifact in the repo, `docker-compose.yaml:12` (`yorkieteam/yorkie:latest`, `command: ["server", "--pprof-enabled"]`), configures no project event-webhook URL/event list, and no script, helm chart or CI step does either (only prose in docs/design/documents-last-modified.md:69). Before this change the per-request admin call produced a real last-modified time with zero extra config; after it, local dev, the Postgres/Yorkie integration lane and any cluster where the `yorkie project update --event-webhook-url` step is skipped will show every doc frozen at its creation time and ordering that never reflects edits. Fix belongs on the new code path: ship the webhook registration as part of deploy/compose config or a startup/ops script rather than a doc note.

findings.summary: Bulk Yorkie maintenance scripts now rewrite every document's last-modified time and scramble the global list ordering
findings.evidence: `migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts:294` (and `migrate-yorkie-cf-ranges.ts:246`, `copy-yorkie-documents.ts:305`) open `sheet-${documentId}` and mutate the root for every document in the workspace. With the new event webhook registered, each of those root changes fires `DocumentRootChanged`, so `touchUpdatedAt` (packages/backend/src/document/document.service.ts:119) advances `updatedAt` for every doc to the migration wall-clock time — the documents list, which now orders by `[{updatedAt: desc},{createdAt: desc}]`, is reshuffled into migration order for all users, permanently. Nothing in the scripts or the webhook path distinguishes maintenance writes from user edits.

findings.summary: `applyGlobalBootstrap` no longer mirrors `main.ts` — it omits the raw-body capture, so no e2e suite can exercise the signed webhook
findings.evidence: The helper's own docstring says it "Mirrors the production `main.ts` bootstrap pipeline … If this drifts from `main.ts`, integration coverage starts lying", yet it only installs the ValidationPipe (lines 75-84). It does not install `bodyParser.json({ verify })`, so any e2e POST to `/internal/yorkie/events` through an app built by the e2e suites (e.g. packages/backend/test/authenticated-http.e2e-spec.ts:72-74) has no `req.rawBody` and gets a blanket 401 regardless of signature. The task doc claims "e2e: signed webhook advances updatedAt" (docs/tasks/active/20260710-docs-list-updatedat-webhook-todo.md:101) but no such spec exists.

findings.summary: Existing controller unit test still stubs the removed `getSummaries` dependency instead of `getEditors`
findings.evidence: `makeController` injects `{ getSummaries: jest.fn() } as never` while `attachMeta` now calls `this.yorkieAdminService.getEditors(keys)` (packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:60). The suite happens to stay green because it only exercises `createDocument`, but the stub is stale and any list-path test added here would blow up with "getEditors is not a function" — the exact trap recorded in docs/tasks/archive/2026/07/20260707-documents-list-sort-search-lessons.md:29.

findings.summary: Frontend `Document.updatedAt` docs now describe the old contract (Yorkie-sourced, absent on single-doc responses)
findings.evidence: packages/frontend/src/types/documents.ts:30-32 says updatedAt is "populated only by the documents-list endpoints (from Yorkie). Absent on single-document / REST v1 responses." Both halves are now false: the value comes from Postgres, and `GET /documents/:id` (packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:136) plus the REST v1 handlers return the whole Prisma row, which now includes `updatedAt`. packages/frontend/src/app/documents/document-list-utils.ts:41-42 carries the same stale "Yorkie's `updatedAt` … when the server had no Yorkie record" description.

findings.summary: Schema design doc's ER diagram for `Document` was not updated with the new `updatedAt` column
findings.evidence: docs/design/backend.md:315-320 lists `id/title/authorID/createdAt` for `Document` (and the surrounding field notes) with no `updatedAt`, while `DataSource` at line 341 does list one. The new column is a schema-contract change other readers/consumers of this diagram rely on.

findings.summary: REST v1 PATCH passes the request body verbatim to `updateDocument`, so the new "don't bump on a no-op" rule is decided by arbitrary body keys, and v1 list ordering was not aligned
findings.evidence: `documents.controller.ts:77-80` calls `updateDocument({ where, data: body })` with the raw `{ title?: string }` body (no DTO class, so the global whitelist pipe does not strip anything). Any non-empty body — including keys that change nothing — makes `Object.keys(data).length > 0` true in the new `updateDocument` (packages/backend/src/document/document.service.ts:100) and re-sorts the doc to the top, unlike the internal controller which builds `data` explicitly (document.controller.ts:183-196). Separately, `list` at documents.controller.ts:29-31 still uses the default ordering, so the v1 surface and the app surface now disagree about document order.

+# Lessons — Documents list `updatedAt` via Yorkie event webhook
+
+## Debug root cause with the live system, not just the code
+
+The two API samples the user pasted were byte-identical and stable — which
+looked like it *disproved* a per-request `updatedAt` flip. Reading the code
+alone couldn't resolve it. `kubectl logs` on the backend pod showed the
+`getSummaries` 800ms timeout firing ~every 5s poll, and a `port-forward` +
+timed `curl` proved the gateway RTT was ~25ms — so the slowness was the
+authenticated presence query straddling the 800ms cut, exactly the flip.
+The identical samples were just two "timeout → fallback" polls. **Measure the
+running system before committing to a mechanism.**
+
+## Don't propose a store you can't fill
+
+The first fix idea ("persist `updatedAt` in Postgres") was hollow until the
+user pushed: edits live only in Yorkie, so Postgres had no signal to write.
+The real design work was *how the value gets there* — the webhook — not the
+column. Verify the data flow feeding a field before proposing the field.
+
+## Verify the external contract from source, not memory
+
+Yorkie's event-webhook contract (event name `DocumentRootChanged`, payload

+# Documents list `updatedAt` via Yorkie event webhook
+
+## Problem
+
+The documents list reorders every ~5s. Root cause (confirmed against the
+live cluster with `kubectl`): the list is sorted by `updatedAt`, which is
+layered on at request time from Yorkie's admin `GetDocuments`. That call
+times out at the backend's 800ms cut on essentially every poll (573
+timeouts / 68h; ~5.8s spacing = every refetch). The gateway RTT is ~25ms,
+so the slowness is the authenticated presence query against Yorkie's
+sharded MongoDB, and it straddles the 800ms cut — so `updatedAt` flips
+between the real Yorkie value and the `createdAt` fallback per poll, and
+the frontend re-sorts each time.
+
+Content edits are recorded **only in Yorkie** (the NestJS backend is not on
+the edit path), so Postgres has no last-modified signal today (`Document`
+has `createdAt` only).
+
+## Approach (Option A)
+
+Feed real edit times into Postgres via Yorkie's **event webhook**
+(`DocumentRootChanged`, fired on actual root-content operations). The list
+then reads/sorts a stable Postgres `updatedAt`; the flaky admin call is
+demoted to editor-avatars only and no longer affects ordering.
+
+Yorkie 0.7.12 contract (verified from source):
+- Event `DocumentRootChanged`; payload
+  `{ type, attributes: { key: "<type>-<id>", issuedAt } }`.
+- Header `X-Signature-256: sha256=<hex>`, `HMAC-SHA256(rawBody, project.SecretKey)`.
+  Signing key = project SecretKey = backend's existing `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY`.
+- At-least-once, throttled per document, retried w/ backoff → receiver must
+  be idempotent + monotonic.
+

+      `@updatedAt`); migration backfills existing rows `= createdAt`.
+- [x] `yorkie-doc-key.ts`: add `parseYorkieDocKey(key) → { type, id } | null`.
+- [x] `DocumentService.touchUpdatedAt(id, at)` — monotonic advance-only
+      (`updateMany where updatedAt < at`), idempotent, no-op on missing doc.
+- [x] HMAC signature guard reading `req.rawBody` + `X-Signature-256`,
+      timing-safe compare against `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY`; reject if key unset.
+- [x] `main.ts`: capture raw body via `bodyParser.json({ verify })`.
+- [x] `POST /internal/yorkie/events` controller (no JWT, signature guard,
+      `@SkipThrottle`): handle `DocumentRootChanged`, parse key, touch;
+      200-swallow unknown keys/other events.
+- [x] `attachMeta`: source `updatedAt` from the DB column; keep `editors`

+---
+title: documents-last-modified
+target-version: 0.5.0
+---
+
+# Documents List — Last-Modified Ordering
+
+## Summary
+
+The documents list orders by "last modified". Content edits, however, flow
+**client → Yorkie only** — the NestJS backend is not on the edit path, so
+Postgres has no edit signal (`Document` historically had `createdAt` only).
+
+The list previously synthesized `updatedAt` per request from Yorkie's admin
+`GetDocuments` call. That call is slow and variable (authenticated presence
+query against a sharded MongoDB) and straddles the backend's 800 ms timeout,
+so `updatedAt` flipped between the real Yorkie value and a `createdAt`
+fallback on each 5 s poll — the list visibly reshuffled. (Confirmed on the
+live cluster: gateway RTT ~25 ms, but the admin query timed out ~every poll.)
+
+This design moves last-modified into a stable Postgres column fed by Yorkie's
+**event webhook**, and demotes the admin call to editor-avatars only.
+
+## Goals / Non-Goals
+
+**Goals**
+- Stable documents-list ordering that still reflects real edit recency.
+- No per-request dependency on the flaky Yorkie admin call for ordering.
+
+**Non-Goals**
+- Self-healing missed webhooks (backend down mid-edit) — accept small
+  staleness; a periodic Yorkie→PG sync can be layered later.
+- Fixing the underlying Yorkie admin-query latency (separate concern; the
+  "currently editing" avatars remain best-effort over it).
+
+## Proposal Details
+
+### Data model
+`Document.updatedAt DateTime @default(now())` — set **explicitly** (not
+Prisma `@updatedAt`). Migration backfills existing rows `= createdAt`. List
+endpoints order by `[{ updatedAt: desc }, { createdAt: desc }]`.
+
+### Ingestion — Yorkie event webhook (yorkie 0.7.12)
+- Event `DocumentRootChanged`, fired on real root-content operations (not
+  presence/attach/watch).
+- Body: `{ type, attributes: { key: "<type>-<id>", issuedAt } }`.
+- Auth: `X-Signature-256: sha256=<hex>`, `HMAC-SHA256(rawBody, project.SecretKey)`.
+  The signing key **is** the project secret key, already held by the backend
+  as `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY` — no new secret. Raw request bytes are captured via a
+  `bodyParser.json({ verify })` hook (HMAC must run over exact bytes).
+- Endpoint `POST /internal/yorkie/events` — no JWT, `YorkieSignatureGuard`,
+  `@SkipThrottle`. Parses the key (`parseYorkieDocKey`), then
+  `DocumentService.touchUpdatedAt(id, issuedAt)`.
+- Delivery is at-least-once, unordered, retried → `touchUpdatedAt` is
+  **monotonic** (`updateMany where updatedAt < at`) and idempotent; unknown
+  keys / other events / missing docs are 200-swallowed so Yorkie won't retry.
+
+### Read path
+`attachMeta` sources `updatedAt` from the DB column and uses
+`YorkieAdminService.getEditors` purely for the avatars. The frontend keeps its
+`updatedAt desc` default sort, which is now stable because the value is.
+
+### Ops
+Register the webhook on the Yorkie project (internal cluster URL, no public
+exposure):
+
+```
+yorkie project update <project> \
+  --event-webhook-url http://wafflebase.wafflebase.svc.cluster.local:3000/internal/yorkie/events \
+  --event-webhook-events DocumentRootChanged
+```
+
+### Non-content updates
+Rename / move never touch Yorkie, so no webhook fires. `DocumentService.updateDocument`
+therefore sets `updatedAt = now()` explicitly on every metadata update, so a
+rename still floats the document to the top like any edit.
+
+### Clock skew
+`issuedAt` is Yorkie's server clock. The webhook clamps it to `min(issuedAt, now())`
+before storing — a future-skewed event must not pin `updatedAt` ahead, which
+(with the monotonic guard) would reject every later real edit until wall-clock
+caught up.
+
+## Risks and Mitigation
+
+- **Duplicate / out-of-order events** → monotonic advance-only update absorbs.
+- **Forged requests** → HMAC signature verification is mandatory; the endpoint
+  refuses to run when `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY` is unset.
+- **`pdf` documents** have no CRDT edits → no webhook → stay at `createdAt`,
+  which is correct.
+- **Backfill of pre-deploy edit history** → the migration seeds existing rows to
+  `createdAt`, discarding any real Yorkie `updated_at`. Low impact in the current
+  deployment (the live admin read times out on ~every poll today, so the list
+  already effectively shows `createdAt` order), but not authoritative against a
+  healthy Yorkie. **Follow-up:** a one-time / periodic reconciliation job that
+  batch-reads Yorkie `updated_at` → `touchUpdatedAt` (Option C) both seeds
+  history and self-heals missed webhooks.
+- **Missed webhook** (backend down mid-edit, or Yorkie retries exhausted) →
+  `updatedAt` stays stale for that doc with no in-app recovery until its next
+  edit. Same reconciliation follow-up closes this.
+- **Deploy sequencing** → the list query reads/sorts the new column, so
+  `prisma migrate deploy` must run before the new image serves traffic, and the
+  Yorkie project webhook must be registered (see ops step) or `updatedAt` never
+  advances. Both are release-runbook items, not code paths.

+# Lessons — Documents list `updatedAt` via Yorkie event webhook
+
+## Debug root cause with the live system, not just the code
+
+The two API samples the user pasted were byte-identical and stable — which
+looked like it *disproved* a per-request `updatedAt` flip. Reading the code
+alone couldn't resolve it. `kubectl logs` on the backend pod showed the
+`getSummaries` 800ms timeout firing ~every 5s poll, and a `port-forward` +
+timed `curl` proved the gateway RTT was ~25ms — so the slowness was the
+authenticated presence query straddling the 800ms cut, exactly the flip.
+The identical samples were just two "timeout → fallback" polls. **Measure the
+running system before committing to a mechanism.**
+
+## Don't propose a store you can't fill
+
+The first fix idea ("persist `updatedAt` in Postgres") was hollow until the
+user pushed: edits live only in Yorkie, so Postgres had no signal to write.
+The real design work was *how the value gets there* — the webhook — not the
+column. Verify the data flow feeding a field before proposing the field.
+
+## Verify the external contract from source, not memory
+
+Yorkie's event-webhook contract (event name `DocumentRootChanged`, payload
+shape, `X-Signature-256` = `sha256=hex(HMAC-SHA256(rawBody, project.SecretKey))`,
+at-least-once + throttled delivery) was read from the pinned `v0.7.12` tag via
+`gh api`, not guessed. The signing key being the *project secret key* is what
+let us reuse the existing `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY` with no new secret.
+
+## Implementation notes
+
+- HMAC must run over the **raw request bytes** — captured via
+  `bodyParser.json({ verify })`, not a re-serialized `@Body()` object.
+- Webhook receivers must be **idempotent + monotonic** (advance-only
+  `updateMany where updatedAt < at`) because delivery is at-least-once and
+  unordered; and **200-swallow** unrecognized input so the sender won't retry.
+- Prisma `@updatedAt` is the wrong tool when the app isn't on the write path —
+  use a plain `DateTime` column set explicitly.

+# Documents list `updatedAt` via Yorkie event webhook
+
+## Problem
+
+The documents list reorders every ~5s. Root cause (confirmed against the
+live cluster with `kubectl`): the list is sorted by `updatedAt`, which is
+layered on at request time from Yorkie's admin `GetDocuments`. That call
+times out at the backend's 800ms cut on essentially every poll (573
+timeouts / 68h; ~5.8s spacing = every refetch). The gateway RTT is ~25ms,
+so the slowness is the authenticated presence query against Yorkie's
+sharded MongoDB, and it straddles the 800ms cut — so `updatedAt` flips
+between the real Yorkie value and the `createdAt` fallback per poll, and
+the frontend re-sorts each time.
+
+Content edits are recorded **only in Yorkie** (the NestJS backend is not on
+the edit path), so Postgres has no last-modified signal today (`Document`
+has `createdAt` only).
+
+## Approach (Option A)
+
+Feed real edit times into Postgres via Yorkie's **event webhook**
+(`DocumentRootChanged`, fired on actual root-content operations). The list
+then reads/sorts a stable Postgres `updatedAt`; the flaky admin call is
+demoted to editor-avatars only and no longer affects ordering.
+
+Yorkie 0.7.12 contract (verified from source):
+- Event `DocumentRootChanged`; payload
+  `{ type, attributes: { key: "<type>-<id>", issuedAt } }`.
+- Header `X-Signature-256: sha256=<hex>`, `HMAC-SHA256(rawBody, project.SecretKey)`.
+  Signing key = project SecretKey = backend's existing `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY`.
+- At-least-once, throttled per document, retried w/ backoff → receiver must
+  be idempotent + monotonic.
+
+## Tasks
+
+- [x] Prisma: add `Document.updatedAt DateTime @default(now())` (manual, **not**
+      `@updatedAt`); migration backfills existing rows `= createdAt`.
+- [x] `yorkie-doc-key.ts`: add `parseYorkieDocKey(key) → { type, id } | null`.
+- [x] `DocumentService.touchUpdatedAt(id, at)` — monotonic advance-only
+      (`updateMany where updatedAt < at`), idempotent, no-op on missing doc.
+- [x] HMAC signature guard reading `req.rawBody` + `X-Signature-256`,
+      timing-safe compare against `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY`; reject if key unset.
+- [x] `main.ts`: capture raw body via `bodyParser.json({ verify })`.
+- [x] `POST /internal/yorkie/events` controller (no JWT, signature guard,
+      `@SkipThrottle`): handle `DocumentRootChanged`, parse key, touch;
+      200-swallow unknown keys/other events.
+- [x] `attachMeta`: source `updatedAt` from the DB column; keep `editors`
+      from the (best-effort) summary. Sort both list endpoints by
+      `[{ updatedAt: desc }, { createdAt: desc }]`.
+- [ ] **Ops (post-merge, needs cluster access)**: register webhook on the
+      Yorkie project (internal svc URL) — see design doc. Until this runs,
+      `updatedAt` stays at `createdAt` but the list is already stable.
+- [x] Tests: `parseYorkieDocKey` round-trip; guard valid/invalid/missing sig;
+      `touchUpdatedAt`/event handling (controller unit). *(DB-backed e2e for
+      the advance-only path deferred; covered by unit + monotonic SQL.)*
+
+## Review
+
+- Backend `build` + `pnpm verify:fast` green (EXIT=0). 20 new unit tests pass.
+- No frontend change needed: the list already sorts `updatedAt desc`; that
+  value is now stable from Postgres, so the flip disappears. The 5s poll now
+  only refreshes editor avatars.
+- Migration `20260710000000_add_document_updated_at` adds the column + backfill.
+
+### Code review (high effort, workflow-backed) — outcomes
+
+Applied:
+- Rename/move now bumps `updatedAt` (`updateDocument` sets `now()`) — a metadata
+  edit floats the doc up; content edits still come via webhook.
+- `rawBody` capture scoped to the webhook path in `main.ts` — no longer retains
+  25MB import buffers on every JSON request.
+- Webhook clamps `issuedAt` to `min(issuedAt, now())` — a clock-skewed future
+  event can't pin `updatedAt` ahead and freeze ordering.
+
+Second review pass (post-fix) — applied:
+- Empty / no-op PATCH no longer bumps `updatedAt` (`updateDocument` skips the
+  bump when `data` is empty), so an empty-body PATCH can't re-sort a doc to the
+  top. Added `document.service.spec.ts` for both branches.
+- Simplified `attachMeta` (`{ ...d, updatedAt: d.updatedAt.toISOString() }`).
+
+Deferred (documented in design Risks):
+- Backfill of pre-deploy Yorkie `updated_at` + self-heal for missed webhooks →
+  reconciliation job (Option C). Low impact now (live admin read already times
+  out ~every poll, so today's list is effectively `createdAt` order); tracked as
+  follow-up.
+- Deploy sequencing (migrate-before-serve, webhook registration) → release
+  runbook items, not code.
+
+## Non-Goals / follow-ups
+
+- Webhook loss self-heal (backend down during edit) — accept small staleness
+  initially; a periodic Yorkie→PG sync (Option C) or read-time touch can be
+  layered later.
+- Live "editing" avatars still use Yorkie presence (decorative; failure no
+  longer affects ordering). Fixing the 800ms admin-query latency itself is
+  separate.
+
+## Verification
+
+- `pnpm verify:fast` green.
+- e2e: signed webhook advances `updatedAt`; unsigned/bad-sig rejected.
+- Manual: list order stable across polls in `pnpm dev`; editing a doc floats
+  it to the top after the next webhook.

+import { Body, Controller, HttpCode, Post, UseGuards } from '@nestjs/common';
+import { SkipThrottle } from '@nestjs/throttler';
+import { DocumentService } from './document.service';
+import { parseYorkieDocKey } from '../yorkie/yorkie-doc-key';
+import { YorkieSignatureGuard } from './yorkie-signature.guard';
+
+/**
+ * Shape of Yorkie's event-webhook body (yorkie 0.7.12,
+ * `api/types/event_webhook.go`). Typed loosely and validated by hand so an
+ * unexpected/extra field never turns into a 4xx — Yorkie retries on failure,
+ * and we would rather swallow-and-200 anything we don't recognize than
+ * trigger a retry storm.
+ */
+interface YorkieEventBody {
+  type?: string;
+  attributes?: { key?: string; issuedAt?: string };
+}
+
+/** The only webhook event type yorkie emits (fired on real root edits). */
+const DOCUMENT_ROOT_CHANGED = 'DocumentRootChanged';
+
+/**
+ * Receives Yorkie document event webhooks and mirrors the last-edit time into
+ * Postgres (`Document.updatedAt`), which is what the documents list orders by.
+ * This is how content edits — which flow client → Yorkie only, never through
+ * this backend — become visible to the list without a per-request Yorkie admin
+ * call. Authenticated by HMAC signature ({@link YorkieSignatureGuard}); not
+ * behind the JWT guard. `@SkipThrottle` so bursts of edit events aren't
+ * rate-limited away.
+ */
+@Controller('internal/yorkie')
+@SkipThrottle()
+@UseGuards(YorkieSignatureGuard)
+export class YorkieEventController {
+  constructor(private readonly documentService: DocumentService) {}
+
+  @Post('events')
+  @HttpCode(200)
+  async handleEvent(@Body() body: YorkieEventBody): Promise<{ ok: true }> {
+    if (body?.type !== DOCUMENT_ROOT_CHANGED) {
+      return { ok: true };
+    }
+
+    const key = body.attributes?.key;
+    const parsed = key ? parseYorkieDocKey(key) : null;
+    if (!parsed) {
+      return { ok: true };
+    }
+
+    // Trust Yorkie's issue time as the edit time, but clamp it to now() and
+    // fall back to now() if missing/unparseable. `touchUpdatedAt` only moves
+    // the time forward, so a clock-skewed *future* issuedAt would otherwise pin
+    // updatedAt ahead and make the monotonic guard reject every later real
+    // edit until wall-clock caught up. Out-of-order / duplicate deliveries stay
+    // harmless.
+    const now = Date.now();
+    const issuedMs = Date.parse(body.attributes?.issuedAt ?? '');
+    const at = new Date(Number.isNaN(issuedMs) ? now : Math.min(issuedMs, now));
+
+    await this.documentService.touchUpdatedAt(parsed.id, at);
+    return { ok: true };
+  }
+}

+import {

+  UnauthorizedException,

+import { ConfigService } from '@nestjs/config';
+import { ExecutionContext } from '@nestjs/common';
+import { createHmac } from 'crypto';
+import { YorkieSignatureGuard } from './yorkie-signature.guard';
+
+const SECRET = 'test-secret-key';
+
+function makeGuard(secret?: string): YorkieSignatureGuard {
+  const config = {
+    get: (key: string) =>
+      key === 'YORKIE_SECRET_KEY' ? secret : undefined,
+  } as unknown as ConfigService;
+  return new YorkieSignatureGuard(config);
+}
+
+function contextFor(
+  rawBody: Buffer | undefined,
+  signature: string | undefined,
+): ExecutionContext {
+  const req = {
+    rawBody,
+    header: (name: string) =>
+      name.toLowerCase() === 'x-signature-256' ? signature : undefined,
+  };
+  return {
+    switchToHttp: () => ({ getRequest: () => req }),
+  } as unknown as ExecutionContext;
+}
+
+function sign(body: Buffer, secret: string): string {
+  return `sha256=${createHmac('sha256', secret).update(body).digest('hex')}`;
+}

+  it('rejects when the raw body was not captured', () => {

+import {
+  CanActivate,
+  ExecutionContext,
+  Injectable,
+  Logger,
+  ServiceUnavailableException,
+  UnauthorizedException,
+} from '@nestjs/common';
+import { ConfigService } from '@nestjs/config';
+import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from 'crypto';
+import type { Request } from 'express';
+
+/**
+ * Verifies Yorkie event-webhook requests. Yorkie signs the request body with
+ * `HMAC-SHA256(rawBody, project.SecretKey)` and sends it as
+ * `X-Signature-256: sha256=<hex>` (see yorkie `pkg/webhook/client.go`). The
+ * signing key is the project's secret key, which this backend already holds
+ * as `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY` for the admin service — so no new secret is needed.
+ *
+ * The raw request bytes are captured by the `verify` hook wired into
+ * `bodyParser.json` in `main.ts`; HMAC must run over the exact bytes, not a
+ * re-serialized object.
+ */
+@Injectable()
+export class YorkieSignatureGuard implements CanActivate {
+  private readonly logger = new Logger(YorkieSignatureGuard.name);
+  private readonly secretKey?: string;
+
+  constructor(configService: ConfigService) {
+    this.secretKey = configService.get<string>('YORKIE_SECRET_KEY');
+  }
+
+  canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): boolean {
+    if (!this.secretKey) {
+      // Without the shared secret we cannot authenticate the caller; refuse
+      // rather than trust an unsigned request to mutate `updatedAt`.
+      this.logger.error(
+        'YORKIE_SECRET_KEY is not configured; rejecting event webhook',
+      );
+      throw new ServiceUnavailableException('Webhook verification unavailable');
+    }
+
+    const req = context
+      .switchToHttp()
+      .getRequest<Request & { rawBody?: Buffer }>();
+
+    const header = req.header('x-signature-256');
+    const rawBody = req.rawBody;
+    if (!header || !rawBody) {
+      throw new UnauthorizedException('Missing webhook signature');
+    }
+
+    const expected = `sha256=${createHmac('sha256', this.secretKey)
+      .update(rawBody)
+      .digest('hex')}`;
+
+    const a = Buffer.from(header);
+    const b = Buffer.from(expected);
+    if (a.length !== b.length || !timingSafeEqual(a, b)) {
+      throw new UnauthorizedException('Invalid webhook signature');
+    }
+    return true;
+  }
+}
